name: upgrade
body:
Upgrade surface: the `kalide upgrade` command and the in-place migration it performs — detect a deck (`kalide.yaml`) or a template library (`library.yaml`) via `detectProject`, decide per kalide-owned file whether to refresh it (present and byte-identical to a known released kalide version in the embedded digest catalogue, or an absent full guide `AGENTS_KALIDE.md`), bring the `AGENTS.md` pointer to the reference scheme (created carrying the embedded pointer content (agent-guide-reference) when absent, migrated from a known released full guide, appended to with the reference line when it is author content without the string, or left untouched when it already carries the string), apply the ordered format migrations defined for the project's version, validate the result, and report every refreshed, migrated/appended and left-alone path.

The `internal/cli` handler `runUpgrade` (internal/cli/upgrade.go) accepts no argument and no `--force`, resolves the current directory with `os.Getwd`, and turns scaffold's outcome into the exit code and user-facing text: success prints the `UpgradeReport` (refreshed and skipped paths) and exits 0; a both/neither project, an unsupported library format, or a failed end-to-end validation prints scaffold's message to stderr and exits 1; any argument is a usage error (exit 2). `cli.Run` dispatches the `upgrade` case to it, beside init, init-library, start, templates, version and help; that shared dispatcher is owned by solution.component.cli-commands.

The `internal/scaffold` entry point `Upgrade` (internal/scaffold/upgrade.go) orchestrates the two halves: detection through `detectProject` and a read-only format guard (`checkSupportedLibraryFormat`) before any write; the never-clobber refresh half `refreshScaffold` (with `refreshReport.refreshMember`/`writeMember` and the seed-vs-external-library predicate `detectSeedDeck`) in internal/scaffold/refresh.go, which owns the guide-pair and `AGENTS.md` pointer decisions, whose permitted modifications are exactly agent-guide-reference's set (creation when absent; appending the reference line to an author file without the string; and upgrade's replacement of a known released full guide); and the ordered, versioned migration half `migrateLibrary` → `runMigrations` over `registeredMigrations` in internal/scaffold/migrate.go. It then validates the result end-to-end through the same loaders `kalide start` uses. An all-or-nothing undo (a whole-tree snapshot for a library, recorded original bytes for the refresh writes) restores the project exactly on failure. The refresh half identifies known versions through the embedded digest catalogue in internal/scaffold/catalog.go (`catalogLookup`); it reuses the embedded guide files and init seed content. The command is local-filesystem only, offline, with no `--force`.
